name: id
desc: Names one element for the whole document. CSS selectors, fragment links, label for attributes and getElementById all use it.
example:
Search results

Jump to results
body:
The value must be unique in the page and must not contain spaces. Two elements with the same id still render, but getElementById returns only the first, and a label for attribute points at the first one too.

CSS matches ids with a hash: #search-results. Keep ids stable, because JavaScript and test scripts depend on them.

name: class
desc: Attaches one or more space separated names. CSS and querySelectorAll use them to style a group of elements, and one element can carry several classes at once.
example: Hotel Belvedere
body: Keep class names lowercase and hyphenated. A class is reusable, an id is not, so style with classes and reserve ids for anchors and script hooks.

name: style
desc: Applies inline CSS to a single element. It wins over most stylesheet rules, which makes it quick for a test and painful to maintain.
example:
Booking cancelled

Booking cancelled

name: title attribute
desc: Adds an advisory tooltip. It also supplies the description for abbr, but it never replaces a visible label.
example:
<abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>

<button title="Close without saving">X</button>
<!-- tooltips do not appear on touch screens, so never hide needed text here -->

name: lang
desc: Marks the language of an element. Screen readers pick the right pronunciation, and browsers hyphenate and spell check with the right dictionary.
example: The German word Zimmer means room.

name: dir
desc: Sets text direction: ltr, rtl or auto. auto lets the browser decide from the first strong character, which suits user generated text.
example:
حجز غرفة

user typed text goes here

name: tabindex
desc: Places an element in the keyboard tab order. 0 means natural order, -1 means focusable by script but not by Tab.
example:
Save draft
...
body:
Avoid positive values. tabindex="1" jumps ahead of the document order and makes the Tab sequence hard to predict.

A div with tabindex and a click handler still announces nothing. Add a role and key handling, or use a button.

name: contenteditable
desc: Turns an element into an editable region. Browsers then accept typing and paste inside it without a form control.
example:
Late arrival, around 23:00.
No pasted tags
body:
The edited text is not submitted with a form. Read element.innerHTML or element.textContent in your script and copy it into a hidden input.

Paste can bring markup, so sanitize the result on the server as well.

name: data-* attributes
desc: Stores custom data on an element without inventing an attribute name. JavaScript reads it through the dataset object.
example:
<button class="book" data-hotel-id="42" data-stars="4">Book</button>

<script>
  const button = document.querySelector('.book');
  // data-hotel-id becomes dataset.hotelId (camelCase)
  console.log(button.dataset.hotelId); // "42"
</script>

name: hidden
desc: Removes the element from rendering and from the accessibility tree. It is a boolean attribute, the same effect as display: none without writing CSS.
example: Check the dates.

name: draggable
desc: Opts an element into the native drag and drop API. The dragged element sets data on dragstart, the target reads it on drop.
example:
Booking A-17
Done

name: spellcheck
desc: Hints whether the browser underlines spelling. Turn it off for booking codes and hex values.
example:
<textarea spellcheck="true" name="description">late arrival</textarea>

<!-- codes are not words, so no red underlines -->
<input type="text" name="booking_code" spellcheck="false" value="BK-2026-0042">

name: accesskey
desc: Assigns a keyboard shortcut, triggered with Alt or Ctrl depending on the platform. Conflicts with browser and screen reader keys make it unreliable.
example:
<button accesskey="s" onclick="document.forms[0].submit()">Save (Alt+S)</button>
<!-- print the hint in the label, users cannot discover the key otherwise -->

name: translate
desc: Tells automatic translation to skip an element. Keep brand names and code samples untranslated.
example:
Book at Hotel Belvedere today.

room_price * nights

name: role
desc: Gives an element an ARIA role when no native element carries the meaning. Prefer a real element, then add a role only for custom widgets.
example:
Booking saved.

...

name: aria-label
desc: Sets the accessible name when the element has no visible text. The name is spoken, so it must not repeat the role word.
example:
<button aria-label="Close dialog">
  <!-- icon only button: the name comes from aria-label -->
  <svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16">...</svg>
</button>

<!-- bad: the word button is read twice -->
<button aria-label="button close">X</button>

name: aria-labelledby
desc: Points at the ids that name the element. It wins over aria-label and over visible text, and it can combine several ids.
example:
Cancel booking

The room will be released.

name: aria-hidden
desc: Removes an element from the accessibility tree while keeping it visible. Use it for decorative images and icons that sit next to a text label.

name: aria-describedby
desc: Adds a hint or error message after the name is announced. Screen readers read it after the label, not instead of it.
example: We send the confirmation here.

name: aria-live
desc: Announces changes inside a region without moving focus. polite waits for a pause, assertive interrupts the current sentence.
example: 2 rooms
body:
The region must exist in the page before the text changes. Creating an element with pre-filled text and aria-live usually announces nothing, because there was no change to observe.

role="status" is polite and role="alert" is assertive. Both imply aria-live, so do not add the attribute twice.

name: onclick
desc: Runs a script when the element is clicked. Inline handlers are quick for demos, addEventListener keeps behaviour out of the markup.
example:
<button onclick="alert('Room held for 10 minutes')">Hold room</button>

<!-- the same behaviour, wired from script -->
<button id="hold">Hold room</button>
<script>
  document.getElementById('hold').addEventListener('click', () => {
    alert('Room held for 10 minutes');
  });
</script>

name: onsubmit
desc: Fires when a form is submitted, whether by button or Enter. Returning false from an inline handler stops the navigation.
example:
<form action="/bookings" method="post" onsubmit="return checkDates()">
  <input type="date" name="start_date" id="start_date">
  <input type="date" name="end_date" id="end_date">
  <button>Book</button>
</form>

<script>
  function checkDates() {
    const start = document.getElementById('start_date').value;
    const end = document.getElementById('end_date').value;
    if (start && end && end < start) {
      alert('End date is before start date');
      return false; // block the request
    }
    return true;
  }
</script>

name: onchange
desc: Fires when a value is committed: on blur for text fields, immediately for selects, checkboxes and date pickers.
example:
<select name="stars" onchange="this.form.submit()">
  <option value="">Any</option>
  <option value="4">4 stars</option>
</select>

<!-- a text field fires change after focus leaves it -->
<input type="text" name="city" onchange="console.log(this.value)">
body: Use input instead when you need every keystroke, for example a character counter or a live filter. change is the event for finished values.

name: oninput
desc: Fires after every change to the value, including paste and drag. It is the event for live counters and search previews.
example: 200 characters left

name: onload
desc: Runs after the page and its images, styles and frames have loaded. DOMContentLoaded is usually the better moment for script setup.

name: onkeydown
desc: Fires when a key goes down while the element has focus. event.key gives the printable name, event.code the physical key.
example:
<!-- key names are readable strings: Enter, Escape, ArrowDown -->
<input id="search" type="search" placeholder="City">
<script>
  document.getElementById('search').addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Enter') console.log('search now');
    if (event.key === 'Escape') event.target.value = '';
  });
</script>

name: onfocus and onblur
desc: Focus and blur fire when an element gains or loses keyboard focus. Neither bubbles, so use focusin and focusout on a parent.
example:
<input name="phone" onfocus="this.select()" onblur="formatPhone(this)">

<form id="booking">
  <input name="city">
</form>
<script>
  // focusin bubbles from the input up to the form
  document.getElementById('booking').addEventListener('focusin', () => console.log('field entered'));
</script>

name: onmouseover
desc: Fires when the pointer enters the element or one of its children. mouseenter fires once per element and ignores children.
example: • Room 101

name: action and method
desc: action is the URL that receives the data, method decides how. GET puts fields in the query string, POST sends them in the request body.
example:
<!-- search is safe to repeat, so GET and a visible query -->
<form action="/search" method="get">
  <input name="city" value="Budapest">
</form>

<!-- creating a booking changes data, so POST -->
<form action="/bookings" method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="hotel_id" value="42">
</form>
<!-- never use GET for passwords, the URL is logged and kept in history -->

name: enctype
desc: Sets how the body is encoded. File uploads need multipart/form-data, the default urlencoded cannot carry binary content.
example:
<form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <input type="file" name="image" accept="image/*">
  <button>Upload</button>
</form>
<!-- enctype is ignored on GET forms -->

name: novalidate
desc: Turns off the browser built in checks so your script can validate and show its own messages.
example:
<form action="/bookings" method="post" novalidate>
  <input type="email" name="customer_email" required>
  <button>Book</button>
</form>
<script>
  // checkValidity still works with novalidate
  document.querySelector('form').addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    if (!event.target.checkValidity()) {
      event.preventDefault();
      console.log('show custom errors');
    }
  });
</script>

name: input type="email"
desc: A text field that expects an address and gets a keyboard with the at sign on mobile. The browser checks the shape, not that the mailbox exists.
example:
<label for="customer_email">Email</label>
<input id="customer_email" name="customer_email" type="email"
       required multiple placeholder="name@example.com">
<!-- multiple allows a comma separated list of addresses -->

name: input type="password"
desc: Masks typed characters. Masking is visual only: the value is plain text in the page, so the form must use HTTPS and POST.
example:
<form action="/login" method="post">
  <label for="password">Password</label>
  <input id="password" type="password" name="password"
         autocomplete="current-password" required minlength="8">
  <button>Sign in</button>
</form>
<!-- use autocomplete="new-password" on a registration form -->

name: input type="checkbox" and "radio"
desc: A checkbox allows several answers, a radio allows one per name. A value is sent only when checked, and a checkbox with no value sends on.
example:
<!-- the same name groups radios into one choice -->
<fieldset>
  <legend>Extras</legend>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="extras" value="breakfast" checked> Breakfast</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="extras" value="parking"> Parking</label>
</fieldset>

<fieldset>
  <legend>Room view</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="view" value="city" checked> City</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="view" value="sea"> Sea</label>
</fieldset>

name: input type="file"
desc: Opens the file picker. The form must use method post and multipart/form-data, or only the filename arrives.
example:
<form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label for="photo">Hotel photo</label>
  <!-- accept filters the picker, it does not validate the upload -->
  <input id="photo" type="file" name="image" accept="image/png,image/jpeg" multiple>
  <button>Send</button>
</form>

name: input type="date"
desc: A date picker whose value is always YYYY-MM-DD. min and max restrict the range and the browser blocks out of range submits.
example:
<label for="start_date">Arrival</label>
<input id="start_date" type="date" name="start_date"
       value="2026-07-01" min="2026-01-01" max="2027-12-31" required>
<!-- the wire format stays YYYY-MM-DD even when the display is local -->

name: input type="number" and "range"
desc: number accepts digits and arrow keys, range draws a slider. Both send a string, so parse before arithmetic. step decides which values are valid.
example:
<!-- range needs a small script to show its current value -->
<label for="adults">Adults</label>
<input id="adults" type="number" name="adults" min="1" max="6" step="1" value="2">

<label for="children">Children</label>
<input id="children" type="range" name="children" min="0" max="4" step="1" value="0">
<output for="children">0</output>

name: input type="color"
desc: A colour picker that returns a lowercase hex value such as #1f6feb. The picker UI is controlled by the browser.
example:
<label for="theme">Card colour</label>
<input id="theme" type="color" name="theme" value="#1f6feb">
<script>
  // the value is always #rrggbb, never a colour name
  document.getElementById('theme').addEventListener('input', (event) => {
    document.body.style.setProperty('--card', event.target.value);
  });
</script>

name: input type="hidden"
desc: Sends a value the user does not see and cannot edit in the UI. It stays visible in the page source, so never store a secret or a trusted price there.
example:
<form action="/bookings" method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="hotel_id" value="42">
  <input type="hidden" name="start_date" value="2026-07-01">
  <button>Book</button>
</form>
<!-- the server must re-check hotel_id and the price -->

name: required and pattern
desc: required blocks an empty submit, pattern checks the whole value against a regular expression. Both produce native messages before submit.
example:
<input type="text" name="booking_code" required
       pattern="[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}"
       title="Two capitals, a dash, four digits, for example BK-0042">
<!-- pattern is anchored automatically: the whole value must match -->

name: placeholder
desc: Shows hint text inside an empty field. It disappears on typing and is not a label, so keep a real label for accessibility.
example:
<label for="customer_email">Email</label>
<input id="customer_email" type="email" name="customer_email"
       placeholder="name@example.com">
<!-- placeholder is not announced as a label by every screen reader -->

name: select multiple
desc: multiple allows more than one option, size sets how many rows are visible. Without size the control collapses to a one line list box.
example:
<label for="extras">Extras</label>
<select id="extras" name="extras" multiple size="4">
  <option value="breakfast">Breakfast</option>
  <option value="parking" selected>Parking</option>
  <option value="spa">Spa</option>
</select>
<!-- a multiple select sends every selected value under the same name -->

name: textarea rows and cols
desc: rows and cols set the visible size in characters, not a hard limit. maxlength limits the value and wrap controls soft wrapping.
example:
<label for="description">Description</label>
<textarea id="description" name="description"
          rows="5" cols="40" maxlength="500"
          placeholder="What should the guest know?"></textarea>
<!-- CSS width and height usually replace rows and cols -->

name: autocomplete
desc: Tells the browser what a field holds so it can fill saved values. Correct tokens on login and address forms save real typing on mobile.
example:
<input type="email" name="customer_email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="text" name="first_name" autocomplete="given-name">
<input type="text" name="last_name" autocomplete="family-name">
<input type="tel" name="phone" autocomplete="tel">
<input type="password" name="password" autocomplete="current-password">
<!-- new-password on sign up, one-time-code on a code field -->

name: fieldset disabled
desc: Disables every control inside the fieldset at once. Disabled controls are skipped in the submit and cannot be focused.
example:
<form action="/bookings" method="post">
  <fieldset disabled>
    <!-- the whole group is locked until payment is confirmed -->
    <input name="room" value="101">
    <button>Confirm</button>
  </fieldset>
</form>
<script>
  document.querySelector('fieldset').disabled = false;
</script>

name: video attributes
desc: controls adds the player UI and poster shows a still before playback. autoplay works only when muted in most browsers, and preload hints how much to fetch.
example:
<video controls width="640" poster="img/hotel-cover.jpg"
       preload="metadata" playsinline muted>
  <source src="media/tour.webm" type="video/webm">
  <source src="media/tour.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  Your browser cannot play this video.
</video>
<!-- playsinline stops iOS from going fullscreen on play -->

name: audio attributes
desc: controls shows play, pause and volume. loop repeats, and preload="none" avoids downloading until the user presses play.
example:
<audio controls preload="none">
  <source src="media/chime.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
  <source src="media/chime.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  Your browser cannot play this sound.
</audio>
<!-- autoplay with sound is blocked until the visitor interacts with the page -->

name: source type
desc: The type attribute lets the browser skip formats it cannot play before downloading. The first source that matches is used.

name: track
desc: Adds a text track to video or audio. captions also describe sounds, subtitles assume the viewer hears the audio.
example:
<video controls src="media/tour.mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="subs/tour.en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  <track kind="captions" src="subs/tour.hu.vtt" srclang="hu" label="Magyar">
</video>
<!-- exactly one default track, the rest appear in the player menu -->

name: picture media
desc: Chooses an image by viewport or format. The img inside is required and supplies the fallback, the alt text and the layout size.

name: iframe sandbox
desc: sandbox restricts what the embedded page may do: no scripts, forms or same origin access unless you allow them. title names the frame for screen readers.
example:
<iframe src="widgets/booking.html"
        sandbox="allow-forms allow-scripts"
        loading="lazy"
        title="Booking widget"
        width="400" height="300"></iframe>
<!-- without allow-same-origin the frame gets a unique origin -->

name: <dfn>
desc: Marks the term being defined in the surrounding sentence. Linking to its id gives other pages a stable anchor.
example:
The average daily rate is room revenue divided by rooms sold.

See average daily rate above.

name: <bdi> and <bdo>
desc: bdi isolates a run of text so its direction cannot reorder the surrounding sentence. bdo forces a direction on its content.
example:
• User إبراهيم booked 2 rooms
  • User Ann booked 1 room
Room 101

name: <ruby>
desc: Places a small annotation above characters, used for pronunciation in East Asian text. rt holds the annotation, rp the fallback brackets.
example:
宿やど means inn.

東京(とうきょう)

name: <wbr>
desc: Marks an optional line break inside a long word or URL. The browser breaks there only when the line is too narrow.
example: Docs: /reference/html-attributes/global

name: <hgroup>
desc: Groups a heading with its subtitle so the document outline keeps one entry. The paragraph is not a heading and is not announced as one.
example:
Hotel bookings

Exam project, 2026

name: <search>
desc: Wraps a search form or filter set. It gives the region a search landmark without adding a role by hand.
example:
<!-- a search landmark without adding a role -->
<search>
  <form action="/search" method="get">
    <label for="city">City</label>
    <input id="city" name="city" type="search">
    <button>Search</button>
  </form>
</search>

name: <menu>
desc: A list of commands or toolbar actions. It is not the navigation menu of a site, nav with a list is still the right element for that.
